chapters.title: Establishing Hezkat Tashmishin
chapters.about: Usage rights for beams and walls

chapters.title: Rabbeinu Tam and ownership disputes

chapters.title: Hezek Re'iyah on roofs
chapters.about: Privacy between neighbors across a street

claims: Rabbi Harari explores the laws of property usage and privacy, specifically focusing on the requirements for establishing ownership rights through usage and the obligation to prevent Hezek Re'iyah between neighbors. (mentions property usage which is only tangentially addressed in the context of ownership)

The class examines the Gemara's discussion on how beams, plastering, and sukkah construction serve as evidence for usage rights, as well as the specific requirements for building privacy walls on roofs when properties face each other across a public thoroughfare. (describes sukkah construction serving as evidence for usage rights, whereas the class discusses beams used for a sukkah)
summary: Rabbi Harari explores the laws of property usage and privacy, specifically focusing on the requirements for establishing ownership rights through usage and the obligation to prevent Hezek Re'iyah between neighbors. The class examines the Gemara's discussion on how beams, plastering, and sukkah construction serve as evidence for usage rights, as well as the specific requirements for building privacy walls on roofs when properties face each other across a public thoroughfare.
questions: How does using a neighbor's wall for 30 days establish legal usage rights?
Why does building a sukkah on a neighbor's wall create a different timeline for establishing rights than a standard beam?
What is the requirement for neighbors to build privacy walls on their roofs when they face each other across a street?
Can a neighbor be forced to build a privacy wall on their own property if they have already started the work?
How does the obligation to build a privacy wall differ from the Torah requirement of a ma'akeh?
